stem: A pharmacy finds that several dispensing errors occurred during evening cross-coverage when staff repeatedly bypassed a barcode warning. Which proposed QRE analysis best fits the Massachusetts systems approach?

choices.text: Record only the name of the last employee who touched each prescription and stop the analysis there.
Examine the warning design, override workflow, staffing and training patterns, then use the findings to redesign the process.
Ignore the barcode process because technology cannot be considered during QRE analysis.
Analyze only whether the affected prescriptions were paid by insurance or cash.
Wait for another identical error before examining any common system factor.

explanation.core_reasoning: A recurring pattern tied to barcode overrides and cross-coverage calls for systems analysis. Massachusetts CQI looks beyond the last person in the chain to workflow, technology, staffing, training and process changes that can prevent recurrence.

choice_analysis.A: Individual accountability may matter, but stopping at the last handler fails to examine contributing systems.
choice_analysis.B: This proposal connects the observed cluster to concrete technology, workflow, staffing and training causes and to preventive redesign.
choice_analysis.C: Technology is precisely the kind of system factor that can contribute to a recurrent dispensing problem.
choice_analysis.D: Payment method does not explain the repeated barcode-override pattern described in the stem.
choice_analysis.E: The existing cluster already supplies a reason to investigate common causes rather than wait for another event.

related_facts: Clusters of events can reveal system causes more clearly than a single incident.
The purpose of analysis is prevention, not simply assigning blame.
explanation.mpje_trap: When the stem gives you a recurring workflow pattern, follow the pattern instead of focusing only on the final individual.

reasoning_steps: Choose an analysis that links causes to preventive process change
